
# Marketing Calendar

Every campaign is the same beat sheet at different scales. Offsets are counted in calendar days from launch day, written `L0`. Emberwake seasons get the full run; Drift Harbor monthly drops get a compressed one.

## Emberwake season beats

| Beat | Offset | What goes live | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Key art lock | L−28 | Nothing public; art frozen so every later asset matches | marketing |
| Announce | L−21 | Season name, date, one key art, news post | marketing |
| Trailer | L−14 | Gameplay trailer, embargoed press kit to creators | marketing |
| Store-page submit | L−12 | Copy and screenshots into console review | marketing |
| Creator embargo lift | L−3 | Creator videos publish; no build access before this | marketing |
| Launch | L0 | Build live, store page flips, patch notes post | liveops |
| Sustain | L+14 | Week-2 beat: a second creator wave or a mid-season hook | marketing |

Season launch dates and their builds are in [[studio-context]]. Anchor the table to the season's listed launch date, never to "next month."

**Weekend rule.** A beat that lands on a Saturday or Sunday moves to the preceding Friday, never forward. Moving forward compresses the gap to the next beat; moving back only lengthens it.

**Store-page timing.** The refresh is two dates, not one: submitted at L−12 and live at L0. Console edits consume a five-business-day review pass per [[storefront-rules]], and the page must not show season content before the build ships.

## Drift Harbor drop beats

Monthly drops ship roughly the first Tuesday of each month, so the run is compressed and has no press wave.

| Beat | Offset | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Announce | D−7 | In-game message and social post; no separate news cycle |
| Teaser clip | D−4 | 15–20s vertical clip, no trailer cut |
| Creator embargo lift | D−1 | Creator program only; no press embargo |
| Store-page submit | D−10 | Mobile review is faster but not instant |
| Launch | D0 | Build live, patch notes post |
| Sustain | D+7 | Half the Emberwake offset — the next drop is already at D−7 |

## Asset lead times

Counted backward from the beat the asset serves, in working days.

| Asset | Lead time | Blocked by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Key art | 15 working days | Nothing; start first |
| Gameplay trailer | 10 working days to cut lock | A playable build of the content being shown |
| Store screenshots | 8 working days | A release-candidate build at shipped settings |
| Patch notes draft | 3 working days | The release manifest from liveops |

## Sign-off

Three signatures, every beat, no exceptions:

- **Marketing** signs copy — every public word, including the news post and the store fields.
- **Design** signs screenshots, trailer capture, and any footage showing UI.
- **Liveops** confirms the date and the build ID the beat points at.

A beat with two of three signatures does not ship. The common failure is a date nobody in liveops confirmed: the campaign runs on a launch date the build will not meet.

## Showcase blackouts

Platform holders run showcase weeks (PlayStation, Xbox, and the Steam seasonal events). Rules:

- **No announce or trailer beat inside a showcase week, or in the three days after it.** A trailer put out against a showcase week is a trailer nobody watches.
- Launch beats may fall inside a blackout. A launch is a date the build owns; an announce is a date the studio chose.
- **If Gladewick has a slot in the showcase, the showcase is the announce.** Drop the L−21 announce, move the trailer to showcase day, and recount every earlier lead time from there.
- Drift Harbor drops launch inside blackouts freely; only their announce beat moves.
- Showcase dates move. Confirm them with liveops before dating the table.
